bet.dominantBottleneck: The rigid boring bar and coupled lead-screw/change-gear experiments are precision enablers, but the key bottleneck is deciding whether to commit scarce capital to one of three production strategies for the concentrated six-figure block demand. The critical unknown is whether general-purpose machine tools (whose precision also constrains all downstream accuracy) can be made accurate enough and flexible enough to serve both the block workflow and the nearby cylinder/screw needs, versus whether the concentrated demand justifies dedicated special-purpose machines.

bet.nextDiscriminatingTest: Instrument a pilot: use the newly rigid boring arrangement and the lead-screw/change-gear/slide-rest setup to produce a representative lot of the block product (all repeated operations: saw, shape, bore, finish) on general-purpose machines run by current craftsmen, and measure per-piece time, dimensional variability, and yield against the six-figure annual quota. Separately estimate the capital and setup cost of the special-purpose sequential line for the same volume. Compare cost-per-piece and precision-transfer under both, and check whether the same general-purpose machines can then also make accurate large cylinders and repeatable screws for the nearby industries—testing transferability before committing to dedicated machines.

mechanically coupled lead screws, change gears and slide rests for reproducible pitch
metrology/gauges to measure dimensional variability and screw geometry repeatability
enough concentrated customer demand certainty to justify scale-up engineering
mainFailureRisks: precision of the general-purpose machine tools may be insufficient for the block's downstream accuracy requirements, and upstream-machine precision error propagates

high initial machine-design cost may be sunk without guaranteed volume from the single large customer
a locally successful pilot on one operation may not validate the full sequential workflow

routeDecisions.reason: Potentially the lowest unit cost at very large volume, but committing now is premature: precision transfer and transferability to other products are unknown, and its capital cost should only be justified if the general-purpose pilot shows the flexible route cannot meet the six-figure quota cost-effectively.

bet.generalizationBoundary: The general-purpose machine pilot on the block product is only a local test; it demonstrates feasibility for that specific workflow under this workshop's craftsmen and precision baseline. Its extension to accurate large cylinders and repeatable screw geometry must be separately verified using the same mechanical components, and adoption in other factories requires that their skill base and upstream precision match—otherwise the flexible routing result may not transfer.

bet.dominantBottleneck: The causal source of the electrical effect is disputed (animal tissue intrinsic electricity vs. contact between dissimilar conductors), and existing sources are weak/transient, so scaling either theory depends on an interpretable, repeatable source of the effect.
liveRoutesRanked: remove animal tissue and construct a repeated conductor/electrolyte stack
treat the controversy as underdetermined and focus on better measurement before scaling either theory
deepen experiments on intrinsic animal electricity
bet.nextDiscriminatingTest: Construct a purely inorganic repeated stack of alternating dissimilar conductors separated by moist conductive material, eliminating animal tissue entirely, and measure whether repeated (not just transient) electrical effects persist. If they persist, the contact/electrolyte explanation is confirmed and the animal tissue is merely a detector; if they do not, the animal tissue is a necessary part of the causal chain.
requiredComplements: A repeatable measurement instrument (e.g., a sensitive electrometer or frog detector with controlled consistency) to quantify the effect rather than rely on qualitative contraction
Systematic variation of conductor pairs to map which combinations produce the largest and most repeatable effects
Moist conductive medium of controlled composition to rule out chemical/reaction confounds in the stack
mainFailureRisks: The inorganic stack may produce only weak or transient effects that the available detector cannot reliably resolve, leaving the discrimination ambiguous
A successful inorganic stack is a local demonstration and does not automatically prove the same mechanism generalizes to all conductor/electrolyte combinations
Side chemical reactions or oxidation in the moist stack could mimic electrical effects, confounding the causal reading

routeDecisions.route: remove animal tissue and construct a repeated conductor/electrolyte stack

routeDecisions.route: treat the controversy as underdetermined and focus on better measurement before scaling either theory

bet.generalizationBoundary: A successful all-inorganic repeated stack demonstrates that dissimilar conductors plus moist electrolyte suffice to produce repeated electrical effects in this configuration; it does not prove that animal tissue never contributes intrinsic electricity, nor that all conductor/electrolyte pairs behave identically, nor that the effect extends beyond the laboratory scale without design changes.
unresolvedUnknowns: Whether the repeated effect depends on specific conductor pair choices or is generic across dissimilar conductors
Whether the moist conductive material acts merely as a passive conductor or participates chemically/electrolytically in generating the effect
Whether animal tissue, when present, adds any intrinsic contribution on top of the contact effect
Whether the effect strength decays over repeated cycles or stays steady enough to power downstream use
Whether any continuous (non-transient) source can be built from this mechanism beyond short observation windows
